data.description:
## Context

DSO's LLM code review pipeline produces multi-cycle PRs that fail to converge. Empirical evidence (PR #65 escalated to user after 4 rounds with explicit "findings have not converged"; PR #62 oscillated 8->8->6 across 3 rounds; ~10-12 of ~50 post-feature PRs took >2 cycles) traces to four interlocking architectural causes:

1. **Reviewers are fully stateless across cycles.** Cycle-N+1 dispatch passes only the new diff — no prior findings, no prior defenses, no list of fixed/defended items. The only inter-cycle signal is in-band `# REVIEW-DEFENSE:` source comments with 3 lines of evaluator guidance in reviewer-base.md. Defended concerns return under new framing; oscillation-check (literal diff-reversals only) does not catch reframed findings on the same line. PR #65's "Retroactive CREATE silently masks failure" was reframed across rounds 3-4 with the defense already present and ignored.

2. **CI/local parity is broken.** plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review uses a hardcoded 5-line system prompt (dispatch.py L23-30): no severity rubric, no NOT-flag downgrade rules, no REVIEW-DEFENSE evaluation, ignores classifier overlay flags, no opus deep-arch synthesis, schema mismatch (findings[] only — no summary, no escalate_review). Local pass -> CI fail is highly likely; some "review cycles" are pure local/CI divergence, not substantive disagreements.

3. **Tier ratchets up mid-resolution as a side effect of cycle count.** light->standard at PASS_NUM>=2; standard->deep on MAX_ATTEMPTS exhaustion (REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md L945-947, L1072). Each upgrade is a fresh stateless review with a stronger model that finds new things. Cycle bloat is structurally encouraged.

4. **Sustained-disagreement loop has no structured terminator.** Resolution sub-agent's only exit is FIXES_APPLIED, FAIL, or ESCALATE-after-MAX_ATTEMPTS. The loop burns the deep tier (3 sonnet + opus) at least once before user escalation. There is no mechanism for "this critical was defended in cycle N and re-raised in cycle N+1 — arbitrate now against the rubric and bind."

This epic addresses all four through stateful re-review with stable finding IDs, a single-source-of-truth review prompt shared by local and CI, an arbitration tier on sustained disagreement, and decoupled tier selection from cycle-attempt count.

## Success Criteria

1. **Stateful re-review (Strategy B).** Cycle-N+1 reviewer dispatches receive `prior_findings.json` and `defenses[]` as out-of-band context. Findings carry stable IDs (deterministic hash of file + line-range-fingerprint + dimension + normalized-claim). Reviewer schema requires per-finding `prior_finding_id` (nullable) and `relation` (one of: NEW_INTRODUCED, NEW_PRE_EXISTING, RESUSTAIN, REFRAME_OF). Findings with `relation: NEW_PRE_EXISTING` (lines unchanged since cycle N) auto-downgrade to `minor` unless they reference a prior_finding_id justifying re-elevation. NEW_INTRODUCED (lines in cycle-N fix delta) are unrestricted to catch fix-induced regressions.

2. **Single-source-of-truth review prompt (Strategy C).** plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/dispatch.py is replaced with a path that loads the same plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-*.md files used by /dso:review. CI uses the same classifier (review-complexity-classifier.sh, not classifier.py), same overlay dispatch (security/perf/test_quality), same schema validation (write-reviewer-findings.sh equivalent), same NOT-flag rules, same severity rubric, same REVIEW-DEFENSE evaluation, same deep-tier opus arch synthesis. CI delta is limited to `REVIEW_CONTEXT: ci` injection (already shipped in 6da2-4cff) and worktree-vs-CI artifact path resolution. Local-passes-CI-fails class of cycles is eliminated as a structural possibility.

3. **REVIEW-DEFENSE delivery is structured, not in-band, and identical local/CI (answer to user question).** REVIEW-DEFENSE comments are removed from source code. Defenses are recorded in a per-PR durable artifact (proposed: `.dso-review-state/<pr-or-branch-id>/defenses.jsonl`, append-only, one record per defense with fields: `prior_finding_id`, `defense_text`, `code_pointer`, `defender`, `cycle_number`, `timestamp`). Both /dso:review and dso_ci_review read this file and pass it into reviewer dispatches via the same loader. Schema and storage are documented in plugins/dso/docs/contracts/review-defenses.md. Migration: existing `# REVIEW-DEFENSE:` comments in the codebase are extracted into the artifact format on first run of the new pipeline; the inline-comment mechanism is removed from reviewer-base.md L266-275 and from review-fix-dispatch.md guidance.

4. **Arbitration tier on sustained disagreement (Strategy F).** When a finding with stable ID `X` is defended in cycle N (defense recorded in defenses.jsonl) and re-raised at the same severity in cycle N+1 by the reviewer (relation: RESUSTAIN against a defended ID), the orchestrator dispatches a single opus arbiter agent (new agent file: `plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-arbiter.md`). Inputs: the finding, the defense, the reviewer-base.md severity rubric and NOT-flag rules, the cited diff hunks. Output: binding decision (SUSTAIN_FINDING | ACCEPT_DEFENSE) with cited rubric clause. Decision is recorded as a defenses.jsonl record with `arbiter: true` and is binding for that finding ID for all subsequent cycles. Replaces the implicit "MAX_ATTEMPTS -> user escalation" failure mode for the reframing-oscillation case.

5. **Decouple tier from cycle count (Strategy G).** Tier selection becomes purely a function of the deterministic classifier at cycle 1 and never ratchets as a side effect of cycle-attempt-count. Tier upgrade still occurs but only on explicit `ESCALATE_REVIEW` from the resolution sub-agent (intent gap, scope drift, classifier-base mismatch evidence) — not on PASS_NUM>=2 alone. Default tier for diffs in the current "score 3-6" band continues to be standard; weak signals that previously bumped light->standard at cycle 2 are addressed by stateful re-review (Strategy B) instead. Documentation (REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md L945-947, L1072) updated; review.max_resolution_attempts retained as a backstop but rarely reached because Strategy F terminates the dominant pathology.

6. **Validation.** Run the new pipeline against (a) the PR #65 diff (the canonical reframing-oscillation case) and (b) the PR #62 diff (the 8->8->6 oscillation case). Acceptance: each converges in <=2 cycles after stateful re-review + arbitration; arbiter dispatch fires at most once per PR; no admin-merge-with-failure outcome required. Plus run against 3-5 randomly sampled small PRs (single-cycle in old system) to confirm no regression on the easy path.

## Cross-Epic Interactions

- **Resource: reviewer-base.md and code-reviewer-*.md.** Interaction with f61f-7e0a (per-story PR structure) and 6da2-4cff (already closed — severity calibration, NOT-flag, REVIEW_CONTEXT:ci, cited_lines): this epic's stateful-re-review additions and REVIEW-DEFENSE removal must layer on top of the rubric structure introduced by 6da2-4cff. Gate: prior_findings/defenses fields are added in a new schema section that does not collide with the cited_lines and severity rubric sections.

- **Resource: dso_ci_review Python package.** Interaction with the CI parity gap (5d6e-86a9 if open). This epic's Strategy C (single source of truth) supersedes any partial parity work; if 5d6e-86a9 is in flight, scope coordination required. Gate: dispatch.py is deprecated/deleted in favor of agent-file loading.

- **Resource: review-fix-dispatch.md and resolution loop.** Resolution sub-agent must be updated to consume defenses.jsonl when proposing fixes/defenses (so it can recognize "this is the same concern as a prior-cycle defense"). Gate: review-fix-dispatch.md L82 minor-defense prohibition retained.

- **Resource: oscillation-check skill.** Current SKILL.md detects literal diff reversals only. This epic's stable-finding-IDs may make oscillation-check redundant (the RESUSTAIN-against-defended-ID detection in Strategy B subsumes it). Gate: assess deprecation in implementation plan.

- **Resource: REVIEW-WORKFLOW-HUGE.md FALLBACK path.** If Strategy E from the per-story epic (f61f-7e0a) ships region-split with dedup, that pipeline must consume defenses.jsonl too. Gate: defenses loader is region-aware (defenses scoped by file path filter through to the right region reviewer).

- **Resource: storage location for defenses.jsonl.** Choice between (a) `.dso-review-state/` in repo (committed; survives rebases; visible in PR diff), (b) tickets-tracker comments (not in-repo; survives across worktrees but adds tracker-load), (c) ephemeral `/tmp` (lost on rebase). Gate: design decision recorded in implementation plan; preference (a) for durability and PR-visibility, but trades off committing review metadata into the codebase.

## Dependencies

- Sequence after f61f-7e0a (per-story PR structure) only if A's size gate is required to make stateful re-review tractable; otherwise can ship in parallel. Most likely parallel — stateful re-review benefits both story-level and epic-level review.
- Coordinate with any in-flight CI parity work to avoid double-implementation of dispatch.py rework.
- Soft dependency on REVIEW-WORKFLOW-HUGE.md region-split work (Strategy E in f61f-7e0a) for the defenses loader to be region-aware.

## Approach

Stateful-re-review substrate first (Strategy B) — it is the foundation for the other three. CI parity (Strategy C) is an independent track and can ship in parallel; it eliminates a whole class of phantom cycles immediately. Arbitration tier (Strategy F) requires the stable-ID substrate from B and so sequences after. Tier-decoupling (Strategy G) is documentation + small workflow logic edits; ships last to avoid disrupting the resolution loop while B is in flight.

Storage decision for defenses: prefer in-repo `.dso-review-state/` for durability and PR-visibility; design implementation plan task to evaluate trade-off explicitly with a written rubric.

REVIEW-DEFENSE inline-comment removal: yes, removable once the structured channel exists, AND the structured channel is mandatory for both /dso:review and dso_ci_review (Strategy C ensures this is structurally enforced, not just documented). Migration: one-time scan + extract on first run of the new pipeline; reviewer-base.md L266-275 deleted; review-fix-dispatch.md updated to write structured records, not insert comments.

## Open Questions for Brainstorm

- Storage location for defenses.jsonl (in-repo vs tracker vs ephemeral) — implementation-plan task with explicit rubric
- Stable finding ID hash inputs — exact specification of "normalized claim" (token-set? embedding similarity threshold? deterministic LLM rewrite to canonical form?)
- Arbiter agent's handling of partial-acceptance ("severity should drop from critical to important but not be dismissed") — binary SUSTAIN/ACCEPT or trinary?
- Fallback when arbiter itself disagrees across two runs (non-determinism risk on opus) — single dispatch with seed pin, or quorum-of-3?
- Whether the resolution sub-agent should see arbiter outcomes from prior cycles to avoid re-defending lost arguments
data.title: Stateful re-review with CI/local parity, arbitration, and tier-decoupling
